messages:
maya: Heads-up — I ran the nightly fp8 perf sweep on H100 and saw a weird throughput + correctness drift around seq_len=2048 when using the new transformer-engine fused kernels. Dashboard: https://perf.redwood.local/d/abcd123/fp8-sweeps :sadpanda:

aj: can you paste the exact command/config you used? did you enable KV caching?

maya: repro command:
```
./bench --model redwood-v1 --device h100 --precision fp8 --kernels fused_te --seq-len 2048 --batch 8 --kv-cache on --warmup 20 --iter 200
```
I also toggled `TE_FWD_PREFETCH=1` and saw slight differences.

pablo: did you run with the new kernel selector or forced kernel? we had a fallback flip last week.

maya: I used auto-selector. If I force `--kernels te_fused_v2` the instability goes away but throughput drops ~12%. If I force `--kernels te_unfused` correctness is fine and throughput is stable (but lower).

sarah: any stack traces or device-side OOMs?

maya: No OOM. Logs show occasional NANs in attention softmax which then propagates. small snippet:
```
[2026-03-15 03:12:01] WARN runtime: nan detected in attn_scores layer_8
[2026-03-15 03:12:01] WARN runtime: kv cache write skipped idx 1023
```
I suspect quantization scale calibration interacting badly with fused kernels at that sequence boundary.

aj: interesting. we saw earlier that calibration (per-channel vs per-tensor) changes ranges variance; maybe fused kernel assumes a particular ordering for scales?

pablo: also check mixed-batching. Are these requests all same-batch-length? selector may pack and the fused kernel has a bug when batch-packed with uneven prefix lengths and kv offsets.

maya: they're uniform in bench, but I tried a real workload trace and saw failures only when there is a small percentage of long-context traces mixed in.

perf-bot: [auto] Regression detected: fp8_h100_fused_te throughput drop of 11.7% vs baseline on nightly-2026-03-14. Linked PR: https://git.redwood/infra/pulls/4123

aj: can you bisect to the PR that changed fused kernel memory layout? suspect commit 7f2c9a2 in runtime/kernels/te_fused.

maya: started a quick bisect, confirmed the problem appears after 7f2c9a2. Reproducer (fast):
```
./bench --model redwood-v1 --device h100 --precision fp8 --kernels fused_te --seq-len 2048 --batch 4 --kv-cache on --iter 50
```
If I set environment var `RW_TE_STRIDE_SAFE=1` things stabilize but perf drops.

pablo: ok that's a strong signal. `RW_TE_STRIDE_SAFE` was added to handle 4-byte alignment assumptions for L40S too. Looks like someone tightened memory packing for perf but broke scale indexing for FP8 fused path.

aj: proposed fix: revert the packing change in te_fused for the FP8 path and add a unit test that exercises mixed-length batching + kv offsets. Also add a calibration test that runs per-channel vs per-tensor and checks for NaNs at seq lengths [512,1024,2048,4096].

maya: I can open a patch and run CI. Also propose a short-term runtime flag to force `te_unfused` for customers on H100/L40S when fp8 is enabled until we ship the fix. Could add auto-fallback in selector when NaNs are detected in the first N steps.

sarah: add to canary plan: run fp8_fused on 5% traffic in us-west with KV caching disabled for the first request per session to see if behaviour persists in production before rolling to 100%.

pablo: also worth noting INT8 kernels didn't show this NaN pattern — so it's specific to FP8 quantization and the fused TE implementation. CI should include an ABI check for scale indices.

aj: thanks — maya, please attach bisect result and the minimal failing test. I'll prioritize a kernel rollback + unit test. Perf team, let's run a calibration sweep (per-tensor vs per-channel) and include telemetry about scale variance per-layer so we can catch this earlier.

maya: filing PR now, will post links. If anyone needs the quick workaround for smoke tests: `--kernels te_unfused --env RW_TE_STRIDE_SAFE=0`.

perf-bot: [note] Canary scheduled: 2026-03-16 08:00 UTC — fp8_fused on 5% us-west. Monitor: https://perf.redwood.local/d/abcd123/fp8-canary

aj: nice. also add a regression alert that triggers if NaN rate > 0.1% over a 10m window.

maya: done, PR 4256 created with tests and rollback patch. will update when CI passes. :thumbsup:
